text: When you have teams naturally break up the world into different funnel stages or different points in the journey, it gets very seductive to look at my part of the funnel and what's my conversion rate through that part of the funnel, right?
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks about growth metrics and team incentives at Shopify. Archie explains a common problem where teams focus on conversion rates for their specific part of the customer funnel. He warns that when teams optimize for local conversion rates as their primary goal, they often inadvertently make it harder for users to reach their stage in the first place, which artificially inflates their conversion numbers but hurts overall business performance.
text_ko: 팀들이 자연스럽게 전체를 서로 다른 퍼널 단계(funnel stages)나 여정의 여러 지점(journey)으로 나누다 보면, 내가 맡은 퍼널 부분만 보고 그 부분의 전환율(conversion rate)만 따지는 데 쉽게 빠져들어요, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 当你的团队很自然地把整个流程分成不同的漏斗阶段(funnel stages)或者客户旅程的不同节点时，就很容易陷入一个误区——只盯着自己负责的那部分漏斗，只关心我这一块的转化率怎么样，对吧？
text_es: Cuando los equipos dividen naturalmente el mundo en diferentes etapas del embudo o distintos puntos del customer journey, es muy tentador enfocarse solo en mi parte del embudo y preguntarse cuál es mi tasa de conversión en esa parte específica, ¿no?
key_sentence: it gets very seductive to look at my part of the funnel and what's my conversion rate through that part of the funnel
original_text: When you have teams naturally break up the world into different funnel stages or different points in the journey, it gets very seductive to look at my part of the funnel and what's my conversion rate through that part of the funnel, right? And then the team starts to optimize for that conversion rate as their north star. But in practice, it's actually almost always easier to just make it harder to do the thing right before your step in the funnel to increase your conversion rate.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage of users who take a desired action, such as making a purchase or signing up for a newsletter, relative to the total number of visitors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In digital marketing and e-commerce, conversion rate is a critical metric used to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing campaigns and website performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high conversion rate is generally positive, it is important to consider the quality of conversions and the overall customer experience.

vocabulary.definition: The distinct phases in a sales or marketing funnel that represent the journey of a potential customer from awareness to purchase.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding funnel stages helps businesses identify where prospects may drop off and optimize strategies to guide them toward conversion.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a narrowing process, where the number of prospects decreases at each stage, highlighting the importance of targeted marketing efforts.

vocabulary.definition: Having an alluring quality that attracts or entices, often leading to a strong desire or temptation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, the term can describe strategies or metrics that are appealing but may distract from broader objectives or critical analysis.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'seductive' can have positive connotations of attraction, it may also imply a caution against being overly captivated by superficial metrics or trends.

text: Most businesses do ultimately fail. And so the way we look at it is can we lower the barriers to getting started and get as many people in the door trying their hand at entrepreneurship?
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks why Shopify seems to optimize for churn rather than retention like most SaaS companies. Archie explains Shopify's unique philosophy around entrepreneurship and business failure. Unlike traditional SaaS companies that want to retain every customer, Shopify focuses on making it easy for people to start businesses, knowing that many will fail but the successful ones will generate massive value that makes the entire cohort profitable.
text_ko: 대부분의 사업은 결국 실패해요. 그래서 우리는 시작 장벽을 낮춰서 가능한 한 많은 사람들이 창업(entrepreneurship)에 도전해볼 수 있게 하자고 봐요.
text_zh: 大部分生意最终都会失败，这是现实。所以我们的想法是，能不能降低创业门槛，让更多人进来试试水，体验一下创业？
text_es: La realidad es que la mayoría de los negocios terminan fracasando. Entonces lo que nosotros nos preguntamos es: ¿podemos hacer que sea más fácil empezar y lograr que más gente se anime a probar suerte con el emprendimiento?
key_sentence: can we lower the barriers to getting started and get as many people in the door trying their hand at entrepreneurship?
original_text: Most businesses do ultimately fail. And so the way we look at it is can we lower the barriers to getting started and get as many people in the door trying their hand at entrepreneurship? If we do that, again, many of those businesses, many of those folks will maybe on their first attempt not be as successful, but we're going to have a set of merchants who go on to become extremely big businesses, the Allbirds of the world, FIGS, etc.

vocabulary.definition: To reduce obstacles or challenges that prevent individuals from entering a particular field or market.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, this phrase often refers to making it easier for new entrepreneurs to start their ventures by minimizing costs, regulations, or entry requirements.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase carries a positive connotation, suggesting inclusivity and accessibility, and is often used in discussions about innovation and economic growth.

vocabulary.definition: The process of starting and managing a new business venture, typically characterized by innovation and risk-taking.
vocabulary.businessContext: Entrepreneurship is a key driver of economic development, as it fosters innovation, creates jobs, and stimulates competition in the marketplace.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with startups, entrepreneurship can also encompass social enterprises and other forms of business that prioritize impact over profit.

text: I think there's probably two things that have been very common. And I would say in quite a few cases, you get a lift on a metric up front, a more short-term metric.
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks about Shopify's practice of running long-term holdout experiments to see if initial positive results hold up over time. Archie explains what they've learned from looking at experiments a year or more later. He describes how many experiments that show immediate positive impact on short-term metrics like conversions or first sales actually show no lasting effect on the business's core metric of GMV (Gross Merchandise Value) when measured over longer time periods.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 아마 두 가지가 꽤 흔한 것 같아요. 그리고 꽤 많은 경우 초반에 지표(metric)가 올라가는 걸 보는데, 그건 주로 단기 지표예요.
text_zh: 我觉得可能有两个比较常见的情况。而且我想说，在很多案例中，你前期确实能看到某个指标有提升，通常是比较短期的指标。
text_es: Creo que hay probablemente dos cosas que han sido muy comunes. Y diría que en bastantes casos, ves una mejora en una métrica al principio, una métrica más a corto plazo.
key_sentence: You get a lift on a metric up front, but no incremental lift later.
original_text: I think there's probably two things that have been very common. And I would say in quite a few cases, you get a lift on a metric up front, a more short-term metric. Number of people who become a paying shopper, number of people who make their first sale in Shopify. And then you look a year later, and there's actually no incremental lift on GMV from that cohort.

vocabulary.definition: A standard of measurement used to assess performance, progress, or quality in various contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, metrics are crucial for evaluating the success of strategies, products, or campaigns, often guiding decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'metric' can refer to any measurement, in business it often implies quantitative data that can be tracked over time.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a limited time frame, typically focusing on immediate results or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, short-term strategies are often employed to achieve quick wins or immediate financial gains, which can be essential for cash flow management.
vocabulary.nuance: Short-term approaches may prioritize immediate results over long-term sustainability, which can lead to trade-offs in strategic planning.

text: I can actually causally change your ability to become successful, because I've given you a little bit more time to try that idea a little bit longer.
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks for an example of experiments that revealed valuable merchant segments that weren't initially obvious. Archie explains how reducing 'monetary friction' - things like trial costs, subscription fees, or other financial barriers - can have unexpected long-term benefits. He describes how providing financial relief to new entrepreneurs can causally impact their success by giving them more time to develop their business ideas and build momentum before giving up.
text_ko: 사실 제가 당신의 성공 가능성에 인과적으로(causally) 영향을 미칠 수 있어요. 제가 그 아이디어를 좀 더 오래 시도해볼 수 있는 시간을 더 줬으니까요.
text_zh: 其实我能直接影响到你能不能成功，因为我多给了你一点时间，让你可以把这个想法再试试看。
text_es: En realidad puedo cambiar tu capacidad de tener éxito de manera directa, porque te he dado un poquito más de tiempo para que pruebes esa idea un poco más.
key_sentence: I can actually causally change your ability to become successful, because I've given you a little bit more time.
original_text: If you think about in a business case, if I give you a little monetary boost and reduce that monetary friction, I can actually causally change your ability to become successful, because I've given you a little bit more time to try that idea a little bit longer. I've given you that opportunity to move your business over to Shopify. And so often in those types of experiments you see that you've basically unlocked a class of people who might've given up without reducing that monetary friction

text: orienting every team to think about the total number of people... who got to the end of their part of the journey is a very powerful way to incentivize people to do the right thing.
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks about Shopify's focus on absolute numbers versus conversion rates as metrics. Archie explains how focusing teams on absolute numbers of successful users rather than conversion rates creates better incentives. He describes the problem where teams optimize local conversion rates by making it harder for people to reach their stage of the funnel, which hurts overall business performance. This misalignment of incentives is something he sees frequently across different organizations.
text_ko: 모든 팀이 자신들이 담당한 여정(journey)의 끝까지 도달한 사람들의 총 수를 생각하도록 만드는 건 사람들이 옳은 일을 하도록 동기를 부여하는(incentivize) 아주 강력한 방법이에요.
text_zh: 让每个团队都去关注有多少用户最终完成了他们负责的那部分流程，这样做特别管用，能让大家主动去做对的事情。
text_es: hacer que todos los equipos se enfoquen en cuánta gente realmente llegó hasta el final de su parte del proceso es una forma muy efectiva de motivar a la gente a hacer lo correcto.
key_sentence: Orienting every team to focus on total people incentivizes doing the right thing.
original_text: And because we focus on that long-term GMV, number of merchants who are successful, orienting every team to think about the total number of people, not the rate, but the total number of people who got to the end of their part of the journey is a very powerful way to incentivize people to do the right thing in terms of getting people set up versus do the, 'I'm going to constrict the funnel step right before me to make my local conversion rate look better,' which is the bane of my existence but something I see a lot of teams, implicitly or explicitly do when they get too focused on rates as a way to think about the world.

vocabulary.definition: To provide motivation or encouragement for someone to take a specific action or achieve a desired outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, incentivizing employees or customers often involves offering rewards, bonuses, or recognition to drive performance and engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'incentivize' is commonly used in motivational contexts, it can imply a transactional relationship where actions are driven by external rewards rather than intrinsic motivation.

vocabulary.definition: The process of aligning or directing someone or something towards a specific goal or understanding.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, orienting teams involves providing them with the necessary information and guidance to align their efforts with the organization's objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'orienting' often implies a supportive and educational approach, contrasting with more directive or authoritative methods.

vocabulary.definition: Having great strength, influence, or effectiveness in achieving a desired result.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, describing a strategy or tool as 'powerful' often indicates its significant impact on performance, decision-making, or competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'powerful' can carry a positive connotation, but it may also imply a potential for misuse or overreach if not managed responsibly.

text: And in practice, I talked about it's actually almost always easier to just make it harder to do the thing right before your step in the funnel to increase your conversion rate.
speaker: Archie Abrams
context: Lenny asks Archie to elaborate on his philosophy about absolute numbers versus conversion rates in growth metrics. Archie provides a concrete example of how teams can game conversion rates by making earlier steps in the funnel more difficult. He explains that by making signup harder, fewer people will sign up, but those who do will be higher intent, which artificially increases the signup-to-activation conversion rate while actually hurting the business by reducing total activated users.
text_ko: 실제로 제가 말했듯이, 전환율(conversion rate)을 높이려면 퍼널(funnel)에서 해당 단계 바로 앞의 행동을 일부러 더 어렵게 만들어 놓는 게 거의 항상 더 쉬워요.
text_zh: 实际操作中我发现，要提高转化率的话，往往最简单的办法就是让用户在你这一步之前的那个环节更难操作一些。
text_es: Y en la práctica, de lo que hablé es que casi siempre es más fácil hacer que el paso anterior en tu embudo (funnel) sea más difícil para aumentar tu tasa de conversión.
key_sentence: Making it harder to do the thing increases conversion rate through higher intent.
original_text: And in practice, I talked about it's actually almost always easier to just make it harder to do the thing right before your step in the funnel to increase your conversion rate. If I make it harder to sign up, it's going to be very easy to increase sign up to activated rate, because I just have fewer people and the people who made it through our higher intent.

vocabulary.definition: The percentage of users who take a desired action out of the total number of visitors to a site or application.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and marketing, the conversion rate is a critical metric used to evaluate the effectiveness of campaigns and user engagement strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high conversion rate is generally positive, it is important to consider the quality of the conversions and the overall customer experience.

vocabulary.definition: A model that illustrates the journey potential customers take from awareness to purchase, often depicted as a narrowing pathway.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales and marketing, the funnel helps businesses understand where they may be losing potential customers and how to optimize each stage of the buying process.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'funnel' can imply a sense of filtering, where only a fraction of leads convert to sales, highlighting the importance of nurturing prospects.

vocabulary.definition: To become or make greater in size, amount, intensity, or degree.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'increase' often refers to growth in sales, revenue, or market share, and is a key objective for companies aiming to expand.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'increase' is straightforward but can imply different strategies, such as organic growth versus aggressive expansion tactics.
